core_obligations: Reduce to one affine piece outside U (proof lines 3074-3087): let n be the minimal number of affine opens needed to cover X together with U; proving the case n = 1 allows one to extend successively over the pieces, so one reduces to n = 1.

Reduce to an affine scheme (proof lines 3089-3097): if X = U union V with V affine then the intersection of U and V is a quasi-compact open because X is quasi-separated; it suffices to solve the problem on V for the restricted subsheaf, since the result glues to the given subsheaf over U along the common restriction, so one reduces to X affine.

Finish on an affine scheme (proof lines 3099-3110): write the given quasi-coherent module as the module attached to an R-module M, use the trivial extension lemma to find a quasi-coherent subsheaf H restricting to G, write it as the module attached to N, and for each point of U choose f with D(f) contained in U and N_f finitely generated; since U is quasi-compact, finitely many such localizations cover U, and the submodule of N generated by the finitely many numerators defines the required finite type subsheaf.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a cover of X by U and one affine open, then to an affine base by glueing.
On an affine scheme produce a quasi-coherent subsheaf restricting to the given one.
Use finite generation after localizing at finitely many elements to cut down to a finite type subsheaf.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme X, a quasi-compact open U and a finite type quasi-coherent subsheaf G of F restricted to U, there is a finite type quasi-coherent subsheaf of F restricting to G (statement lines 3063-3072). The proof (proof lines 3074-3112) reduces to one affine piece outside U and then to an affine base by glueing, produces a quasi-coherent subsheaf there, and cuts it down to a finite type subsheaf by localizing at finitely many elements covering U. H2: a two-step reduction with an explicit finite generation argument, written out in full.
